text:
Ava (CFO): Thanks for coming to the all-hands today. Dropping a follow-up thread for runway/burn questions and operational clarifications. Please post quick Qs and we’ll answer here. :sparkles:

morgan (eng): Quick one — how are we defining runway now? Is it still months of runway at current burn or adjusted for expected hiring?

Ava (CFO): We publish runway as 'months at projected burn', which includes approved hiring in the next quarter + committed reserved capacity (Dedicated). We use a 3-month trailing average to smooth spikes.

alex (product): Will that projected burn include the new dedicated infra purchase we quoted last week?

Ravi (Finance Ops): Yes — any committed vendor contracts or reserved capacity that have been approved by Purchasing/Finance are included. If a purchase is still in approval, it's excluded until PO is issued.

jamal (sales): Are we changing hiring pace? Heard different things in PM sync.

Sofia (People): No hiring freeze. We are aligning hiring with role prioritization. Sr-level roles still go through an additional calibration with hiring committee for Q2.

morgan (eng): For procurement timing: vendors onboarded last quarter saw 3–4 week delays. Any plan to speed that up?

olivia (procurement): We're piloting a "fast-track" vendor SLA for infra & critical cloud partners: target onboarding 7 business days if vendor provides standard MSS and certs. For bespoke/legal review it can take longer. Please tag me on tickets.

morgan (eng): Nice. What's the exact intake path?

procurement-bot: New vendor requests -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/secure/QuickCreate -- choose 'Vendor Onboarding' request type. Status updates auto-post to #vendors.

Ava (CFO): A few more clarifications from finance ops:
- P-card threshold remains $2k for engineers, $10k for managers for non-capex software purchases.
- Any spend > $50k needs pre-approval by Finance + Legal (submit PO request).

alex (product): Can teams self-approve trial SaaS under $500?

Ravi (Finance Ops): Yes, under $500 is self-serve; still record it in the expense tracker (link below) so we can centralize subscriptions.

olivia (procurement): Please use this form for small SaaS: https://forms.gle/rdw-small-saas and include expected MRR + number of seats.

jamal (sales): Question about invoice timing: when should we expect payment runs to clear? Customer invoice vs vendor invoice windows?

Ravi (Finance Ops): Vendor AP runs twice weekly (Tue/Thu). If you need expedite, create a ticket with urgency + business reason. Customer invoicing is monthly EOM; cash receipts are posted as received.

morgan (eng): If a vendor quotes upfront setup fees that push us over the $50k threshold, do we pause until approval?

Ava (CFO): Not necessarily pause — for customer-impacting or safety-critical infra, we have an emergency spend path: create an "Emergency Spend" ticket, tag @Ava and @Ravi. We evaluate same-day and can temporarily greenlight pending formal PO. Use sparingly.

Sofia (People): One more note — any headcount-linked contract must include People in the approval flow (we need start dates for ramp forecasting).

morgan (eng): Appreciate the details. Can finance share the short doc that defines "projected burn" math?

Ravi (Finance Ops): Sure — snapshot and short explainer here: https://drive.redwood.com/finance/projected-burn-qna (contains formula, inputs: salaries, benefits, committed infra contracts, reserved capacity amortized over term).

olivia (procurement): I’ll post a short playbook in #vendors with the fast-track checklist and ticket templates later today.

Ava (CFO): Thanks all. If you have a specific vendor or contract that’s blocking work, reply with the vendor name & ticket ID and we’ll triage. Otherwise, we’ll keep this thread as the canonical Q&A for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
